item.meaning: A flat, fertile landform created by nutrient-rich silt and sediment deposited by flowing rivers over millennia.
An ancient Tamil Sangam literary classification mapping ecological landscapes to human emotions and livelihoods.

item.title: Geological Formation of Landforms
item.explanation: Internal tectonic forces uplift land to form mountains and plateaus, while external weathering and fluvial erosion carve valleys and deposit fertile alluvial plains.

item.cause: Tectonic plate movements and internal Earth forces
item.effect: Crustal uplift forms high mountain ranges (e.g. Himalayas) and elevated plateaus.

item.cause: Erosion and silt deposition carried by major river systems like the Ganga and Indus
item.effect: Formation of vast, highly fertile river plains suitable for dense human habitation and intensive agriculture.

item.category: The Five Tamil Sangam Tiṇais (Ecological Zones)
items: 1. Kuriñci: Mountainous zone associated with hunting and gathering.
2. Mullai: Pastoral forest zone associated with cattle rearing.
3. Marutam: Wetland river valley zone associated with agriculture.
4. Neytal: Coastal zone associated with fishing and salt extraction.
5. Pālai: Arid desert zone associated with dryland survival.

item.description: The young fold mountain range forming India's northern natural boundary, acting as a climatic and physical barrier.
